hints: Focus on what Y to Z must be, since adding half a mole of O2 means adding just one O atom per molecule of Y.
Try the nitrogen case first with Y as NO forming NO2 in the atmosphere, then check oxidation numbers and electrons.
Now test the sulfur case with Y as SO2 forming SO3, and ask which statements stay true for at least one choice of X.
walkthrough:
**Work out the Y to Z change**

Think simply first. 1 mol of Y plus 0.5 mol of $\text{O}_2$ means 1 atom of O is added per molecule of Y.

So the reaction is:
$$\text{Y} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{Z}$$

**Identify the two possible pollutant pairs**

In a car engine, nitrogen gives $\text{NO}$ and sulfur impurities give $\text{SO}_2$. Both are further oxidised in air.

$$2\text{NO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2$$
$$2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{SO}_3$$

**Test statement 1 about oxidation number**

Oxygen is -2, so adding one O raises the oxidation number of X by +2 to balance it.

For nitrogen: $\text{NO}$ (+2) to $\text{NO}_2$ (+4). For sulfur: $\text{SO}_2$ (+4) to $\text{SO}_3$ (+6). Statement 1 is true.

**Test statements 2 and 3 and conclude**

$\text{NO}$ has 5 + 6 = 11 outer electrons, so it must have an unpaired electron. $\text{SO}_2$ has all electrons paired, so statement 2 is true for X = nitrogen.

Both $\text{NO}$ (heteronuclear diatomic) and $\text{SO}_2$ (bent) are polar, so statement 3 is true. Since all three can be true together when X is nitrogen, 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

options.A: Correct, because when X is nitrogen, Y is NO and Z is NO2. Oxidation number rises from +2 to +4 (increase of 2), NO is a radical with an unpaired electron, and NO is polar. All three statements can be correct together.
options.B: Incorrect, because it leaves out statement 3. Both possible Y molecules, NO and bent SO2, are polar, so there is no reason to exclude statement 3.
options.C: Incorrect, because it leaves out statement 1. Adding one O atom always increases the oxidation number of X by 2, as seen in NO to NO2 and SO2 to SO3.
options.D: Incorrect, because it claims only statement 1 is correct. This ignores that NO clearly has an odd electron count and is polar, so statements 2 and 3 can also be correct.
